paper_metadata.title: Scheduling process of quantum circuits to optimize tasks execution on quantum computers

experiments.description: Validation of the proposed quantum circuit scheduling process using a mixed batch of 10 gate-based quantum algorithms executed as combined circuits on IBM Quantum and Amazon Braket, compared against individual executions.

algorithm.variant: Mixed benchmark of 10 gate-based algorithms: Berstein-Vazirani, Deutsch-Jozsa, Full Adder, Grover, Kickback, Phase Estimation, Quantum Walk, Shor, Simon, and Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP)

hyperparameters.cycle_definition: finite period waiting for more circuits or until available qubits are completed

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Circuits were submitted either as Quirk simulator URLs or as Python code repositories in Qiskit or Braket; the scheduler remapped each circuit to disjoint qubit ranges on the target machine.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Circuits were packed into a single execution while ensuring qubits were not shared between circuits; results were later unscheduled by splitting measured bitstrings according to assigned qubit ranges.

problem_instance.description: A benchmark suite of 10 quantum algorithm implementations from Zenodo used to test the scheduling process under different circuit compositions and shot settings.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Zenodo public repository of quantum circuits

dataset_specification.description: Repository DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.11633677; algorithms included Berstein-Vazirani, Deutsch-Jozsa, Full Adder, Grover, Kickback, Phase Estimation, Quantum Walk, Shor, Simon, and TSP; used in different scheduling test compositions.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No classical data preprocessing reported; circuits were adapted to the target hardware topology during transpilation and qubit assignment.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of scheduled execution versus individual execution; execution cost and runtime were measured, and noise impact was assessed using Wasserstein distance between output probability distributions.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Quantum hardware topology and gate set
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Unscheduling of combined measurement results into per-circuit outputs; Wasserstein distance used for comparison against individual runs.

speedup_claims.conditions: average scheduled execution time of 20 seconds versus average sum of individual executions of 80 seconds
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as average wall-clock time; scheduling time is close to the deepest circuit execution time.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: individual execution cost on Amazon Braket
speedup_claims.caveats: Cost reduction is proportional to the number of qubits used in the total scheduling.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: individual execution cost on IBM Quantum
speedup_claims.caveats: Cost reduction is proportional to the number of qubits used in the total scheduling.

complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: Average scheduled execution time reported as 20 seconds
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: Average sum of individual executions reported as 80 seconds
